titulo: Never Kill the Spider in Your Ceiling Corner. It Hunts Black Widows
titulos_alternativos: Never Kill This Spider. It Eats Black Widows for You
The Fragile Spider That Beats Black Widows
descripcion:
It is two in the morning, you flip on the light, and there it is: a tiny pale spider with impossibly long legs, hanging in a dusty web in the corner of the ceiling. Your first instinct is to grab the broom. Don't.

The cellar spider (the one most people call daddy longlegs) is one of the best bodyguards your house can have. It hunts other spiders, including black widows.

In this video:
- The three different animals people call daddy longlegs
- Why that messy web is really a trap and an alarm system
- How a fragile spider beats a black widow from a distance
- The sneaky trick it uses to lure other spiders out (aggressive mimicry)
- Its strangest defense: whirling until it turns into a blur
- The myth of the most venomous spider in the world
- A mother that carries her eggs in her mouth
- How to tell a cellar spider from a black widow in two seconds
- What to do if you find one (and why bug spray backfires)
